explain.say: When you cut your skin, tiny blood vessels break and bleed. Within minutes your body seals the gap, and the scab you see is the roof over a busy repair site.

explain.say: Platelets and a net of fibrin threads form a clot that plugs the cut. As it dries, the clot hardens into a scab, a natural plaster that keeps out dirt and germs.

explain.say: Underneath, white blood cells arrive. They swallow germs, dirt and damaged cells, which is why a healing cut can look a little red and puffy at first.

faq.a: Platelets stick together at the cut and a protein called fibrin weaves a net that traps blood cells into a clot. On the surface the clot dries out and hardens into a scab.
asks: What is a scab made of?
Why does a cut get a scab?

faq.a: A scab is a protective crust over the wound. It keeps dirt and germs out and protects the delicate new tissue growing underneath until the skin has closed.
asks: Why shouldn't you pick a scab?

faq.q: What do white blood cells do in a healing cut?
faq.a: First, white blood cells called neutrophils rush in to kill germs. Then larger cells called macrophages eat dead cells and debris and release signals that start the rebuilding.
asks: Why does a cut go red and puffy?
How does the body clean a wound?

faq.q: How does skin grow back under a scab?
faq.a: Skin cells at the edges of the wound multiply and creep across the damaged area under the scab. Below them, cells called fibroblasts make new collagen and new blood vessels grow in.
asks: How does a cut close up?

faq.q: Why do scabs fall off on their own?
faq.a: Once new skin has covered the wound, the scab is no longer attached to living tissue, so it loosens and falls off. Picking it early can tear the new skin and slow healing.
asks: When does a scab come off?
Why does a scab peel off?

facts: Neutrophils are usually the first white blood cells to arrive in a wound, followed by macrophages.
New skin can grow in from the edges of a wound and from stem cells in surviving hair follicles.

quiz.say: What is the main job of a scab?

options.show: Protects the wound while new skin grows
options.say: Protects the wound while new skin grows

options.show: Stops the skin from ever scarring
options.say: Stops the skin from ever scarring

quiz.why: The scab is a protective crust that keeps germs and dirt out while the skin repairs underneath.

wrong.1: New blood cells are made in bone marrow, not in a scab.
wrong.2: Whether a scar forms depends on how deep the wound was, not on the scab.
